by_task.when: ILLINOIS is allowable and the property is held for personal rather than business use.
by_task.procedure: Evaluate 735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001(b) independently as the any-other-property alternative, including when apparel, a motor vehicle, or a prescribed health aid also has a specific exemption. Section (a) covers necessary wearing apparel, (c) covers a motor vehicle, and (e) covers professionally prescribed health aids. A value above a limit does not eliminate either applicable alternative.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not use § 12-1001(d) for ordinary household property; it requires implements, professional books, or tools of the debtor's trade. Do not classify jewelry or a watch as necessary wearing apparel under subsection (a), and do not omit subsection (b) merely because a specific subsection applies. Subsection (b) is a personal-property exemption; do not apply it to any real-property interest.

by_task.when: ILLINOIS is allowable and the debtor owns personal-use property.
by_task.procedure: Determine eligibility before calculating amounts. Independently include § 12-1001(b) for any debtor-owned personal-use property, including property also covered by subsection (a), (c), or (e); a value above its ceiling does not defeat eligibility. Use the lesser of value and $4,000 for one debtor or $8,000 for jointly owned property of two debtors. For a motor vehicle, also report subsection (c) at the lesser of value and $2,400, without doubling that limit. Sections (a) and (e) use the asset value because the supplied text states no dollar ceiling.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not use subsection (d) merely because an item could be called a tool or implement; require facts showing use in the debtor's trade. Do not classify jewelry as necessary wearing apparel, omit subsection (b) because a specific subsection applies, treat either ceiling as an eligibility test, or apply these exemptions to business-use property. Subsection (b) applies only to personal property, not to any real-property interest.

operations.rationale: In source 281, the parent correctly used § 12-1001(b) for the debtor's personal property but also extended it to a real-property interest. The supplied statute confines § 12-1001 to personal property. This narrow boundary correction removes that false positive while preserving the existing overlap, category, cap, and trade-use instructions verbatim.
